Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. A few follow-ups from the security & compliance team at MedOnco. We're evaluating Redwood for storing and processing PHI-adjacent clinical annotations; residency is a hard requirement for most of the datasets. We need clarity on three items before we proceed to a procurement review: 

1) Scope decomposition: for an APAC "pin" can you confirm what classes of data are guaranteed to remain in-region (raw payloads, model inputs, KV/cache, logs, telemetry)? We need this at the field/asset level (e.g., patient identifiers vs. anonymized text).

2) Temporary replication/egress: we accept limited failover windows for high-availability, but we need the exact conditions (duration, notification, encryption in-flight & at-rest, and whether egressed tokens are scrubbed/rotated).

3) Subprocessor roster & KMS: please provide an up-to-date APAC subprocessor roster and confirm whether customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported for the APAC region. If not, what escrow or key-separation controls exist?

We're trying to avoid a long legal DPA back-and-forth — providing a scoped technical playbook and the roster would help accelerate sign-off. Can you loop in legal/security and share a single-page summary plus any CSV roster?

Best,
Elaine Tan
Director, Cloud Security
MedOnco Inc

Elaine —

Thanks for the clear asks; putting concise answers and an action plan below. Looping Marissa (legal) and Kim (reliability/security) to add the contractual and technical artefacts.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Scope decomposition: Redwood can pin customer data to APAC at the request of the account. We separate four logical stores: (1) customer payloads, (2) model input tokens/KV cache, (3) operational logs/metrics, (4) long-term audit logs. For APAC pin, payloads, model inputs/KV, and audit logs can be restricted to APAC. Operational metrics are aggregated and may be processed in our central telemetry pipeline unless you opt out; we can provide a reduced telemetry mode.

- Temporary replication/egress: we support transient replication for failover. Default max window is 60 minutes; we have a configurable SLA clause for up to 4 hours with advance notification. All replicated data is TLS-encrypted in-flight and AES-256 encrypted at-rest in the target region. During replication we rotate session tokens and scrub ephemeral keys upon failback. We'll provide a playbook listing the exact trigger conditions and notification cadence.

- Subprocessors & KMS: attached is our current APAC subprocessor roster CSV. We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in APAC for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers may use Redwood-managed keys with an HSM-backed KMS. We also offer an escrow option where we provide key-wrapping evidence for audit.

Next steps: Marissa & Kim will send a 1-page scoping summary + technical playbook and a roster CSV. Can you confirm whether MedOnco needs BYOK (customer-supplied) for production or if an HSM-backed Redwood key is acceptable for an initial pilot?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine —

Marissa here from Legal & Compliance. Thanks for the precise list — below is a compact, contract-oriented response you can share with procurement. I've also attached the APAC roster and a temp-egress playbook (stubs).

1) Residency guarantees (contract language we propose):
- "Customer Data" for the APAC pin shall be stored and processed within APAC data centers and shall not be intentionally replicated outside the APAC region except for documented, time-bound HA failover events described in the Temporary Egress Playbook.
- "Customer Data" excludes aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics (see telemetry appendix).

2) Temporary egress:
- Triggers: region outage or islanding that impacts >20% of customer-requested capacity for >5 minutes.
- Maximum egress duration for hosted customers: 60 minutes (default) unless a mutually agreed extension is executed. For Dedicated/Private customers these durations are configurable in the SOW.
- Notification: automated alert to designated DPO + 15 minute post-trigger human call.
- Controls: all data encrypted in transit; egress endpoints limited to pre-approved, audited subprocessors; logs of all egress actions are retained in-region and exported as a redacted – for audit.

3) Subprocessor roster & KMS:
- Attached: "regional_subprocessor_roster.csv" (includes vendor name, location, role, SOC/ISO references).
- BYOK: Supported for Dedicated/Private in APAC. For hosted customers in APAC we offer an HSM-backed Redwood key with dual-control escrow on request. Escrow is available under an addendum and requires a standard escrow SLA.

Documents attached: regional_subprocessor_roster.csv (stub), temp_egress_playbook.pdf (stub), kms-keying-detail.txt (stub).

If the MedOnco DPO needs any specific attestations (e.g., onshore KMS operators, split-key custodian details), Laura from our security ops will coordinate evidence collection.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Redwood Inference
